findings.title: A malformed repo string is treated as "not covered" and gets the platform PAT.
findings.body:
When `normalize_repo` rejects the input, `token_for_repo` returns `None`, the same answer as "the provider does not cover this repo". `resolve_github_token` then returns the platform PAT. So a repo the provider does cover gets the platform PAT, which reaches every repo, if the caller passes it in another form. Examples: `https://github.com/acme/app`, `acme/app/`, `github:acme/app`, or a crafted value like `acme/../x`. This breaks FR-4, which says the platform PAT is used only when the provider answers "not covered". Input that was rejected for safety gets the widest-reaching credential. The new test `test_a_malformed_repo_never_reaches_the_provider` pins this behaviour.

When a provider is registered and the repo cannot be normalized, raise `GithubTokenUnavailable` (or a `ValueError`) instead of returning `None`. The resolver then never hands the platform PAT to input it could not validate.
